cases.question: No wool for this trip to Miami, but I love my wool coats at home. What should I pack?

blocks.text:
Miami Packing

Skip wool entirely and lean into light, breathable layers that handle heat, humidity, and air-conditioning. Pack a small, easy mix rather than a lot of structure.

Tops: Bring mostly lightweight tees, tanks, and one slightly dressier short-sleeve top. Natural-feel fabrics or technical blends that dry fast will be the most comfortable.

Bottoms: Pack shorts or airy trousers, plus one pair of jeans or a sturdier pant only if you know you’ll want them at night. Keep waistbands comfortable and non-restrictive.

Layer: Instead of a wool coat, pack one very light layer for indoor AC: a cotton overshirt, unlined jacket, or thin cardigan if you run cold.

Shoes: Choose your most comfortable warm-weather shoes, and keep it to two pairs max if you can. Miami is better with easy walkable footwear than anything heavy.

Evening piece: Add one polished top or dressier bottom so you can step up for dinner without needing a jacket.

Avoid: Leave wool, heavy knits, and bulky tailoring at home. They’ll read too warm and take up valuable space.

cases.question: Do I need another navy shirt? Be honest about whether it adds anything to my wardrobe.

blocks.text: Honestly: probably not. You already have a navy Oxford shirt in a regular, wearable cut, and with only one other light neutral top showing, another navy shirt is likely to be a duplicate rather than a real addition.

The only reason to buy another would be if you want a meaningfully different role — for example, a lighter-weight navy shirt, a more relaxed overshirt, or a sharper dress shirt. If it’s just another navy button-up for casual wear, I’d skip it.

No — another navy shirt would be redundant in this wardrobe. You already have a navy Oxford shirt, and your closet is small enough that a second navy top would mostly repeat the same role instead of opening up new outfits. What would add more is a shirt in a lighter neutral or a more contrasting color, because your current tops already cover cream and navy cleanly.

If you want the most useful next shirt, I’d look for something like light blue, white, or a subtle stripe. That would pair more distinctly with your olive chinos and dark jeans than another navy piece would.
